- A single punch through folded paper produces one hole per layer, and the holes must mirror each other across the fold line(s).
- Four holes in this rectangular arrangement require the paper to be folded into four layers (quarter size), i.e., folded along the vertical center line AND the horizontal center line.
- Checking option C: folding along the vertical and horizontal midlines stacks four quarters. A punch at one point (e.g., lower-left quarter) unfolds to holes at all four mirror positions: left/right reflections and top/bottom reflections — exactly the pattern shown.
- Options A and D (diagonals) would produce hole patterns symmetric across diagonals, which this is not. Options B and E (vertical folds only) would put all holes on a single horizontal row, which contradicts the two rows of holes.

Therefore, the fold lines correspond to choice C.
